lesson_title: Tip Out the Bags: Adding Powers Has No Law
hook_text: 2 cubed plus 2 to the fourth. Half the class writes 2 to the seventh. Here is why that is 104 marbles too many.
clip_script: Think of 2 cubed as a bag of 8 marbles and 2 to the fourth as a bag of 16. Add them? Tip both bags out and count: 24. There is no shortcut, because the labels tell you how the marbles were made, not how many you have. 2 to the seventh would be 128 marbles nobody owns. Multiplying is different: same base, add the exponents. Same exponent, different bases? 2 cubed times 5 cubed pairs three twos with three fives: 10 cubed, a thousand. Neither matches? Just work it out. And for big numbers in scientific notation, multiply the fronts, add the powers of ten — but to ADD them, the powers of ten must match first, like shelves. Plus sign? Count. Times sign? Shortcut.
visual_style: Two cloth bags labelled 2^3 and 2^4 tip marbles onto a table with a counter reaching 24; a ghost bag labelled 2^7 overflows and is struck out; pairs of 2s and 5s snap into 10s; shelves labelled 10^4 and 10^5 slide to align.
pacing: Fast marbles, a hard stop on the struck-out 2^7, then crisp rules.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and never add exponents under a plus sign again.
